questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.topic: A change notice with no date
questions.learningObjective: Identify when a change notice lacks an effective date
questions.stem: A ticket asks why users saw the new pricing before the announced switch date.

options.text: The notice stated the date but placed it after the change took effect.
The notice used a relative phrase like soon instead of a calendar date.
options.misconception: treats relative wording as precise enough

options.text: The notice omitted the effective date so nobody knew when it applied.
options.misconception: assumes readers infer dates from context

options.text: The notice repeated the old price so users ignored the new one.
options.misconception: confuses price display with timing clarity

questions.explanation: The notice did include a date, but it appeared after the change, so users missed it. Timing clarity requires the date before the action. Relative wording alone would also fail.
questions.hint: Check where the date appears in the notice.
